Fixed colours for groups that stay the same across reports

Source: R/keys.R
phw_colour_key.Rd

A colour key gives every group (an age band, a health board, an organism) its own colour and remembers it. Each time you plot, groups already in the key keep their colour. New groups get the next palette colour that the key isn't using yet. So adding a "90+" age band next month doesn't reshuffle the colours of the other bands.

Usage

phw_colour_key(
  levels,
  name = NULL,
  palette = phw_default_palette(),
  fixed = NULL,
  neutral = default_neutral,
  neutral_colour = phw_colours[["grey_mid"]],
  save = TRUE
)

Arguments

levels

The groups: a factor (its levels are used, in order), or a character vector.

name

Key name, e.g. "age_group". NULL gives colours in order with no memory.

palette

Palette for new groups: a name from phw_palettes, or a vector of colours.

fixed

Named vector of colours to pin, e.g. c(Wales = "#285087"). Pinned colours replace any stored colour.

neutral

Group names to draw in neutral_colour. Matching ignores case.

neutral_colour

Colour for neutral groups.

save

Store new colours in the key?

Value

A named character vector of colours, one per group in levels.

Details

  • In one session, keys live in memory. Use the same name in every chart.

  • Across reports, point phwstyle at a CSV file with phw_key_file(). Keys are then read from and written to that file, which you can keep with the project (and in version control). The file is plain text: key,level,colour. You can edit it by hand.

The key stores the colour itself, not a position in a palette. Changing palette later only affects groups that don't have a colour yet. To move a whole key to a different palette on purpose, use phw_key_recolour().

The one exception is the colour-blind safe "accessible" palette, which can be switched on for a whole document (see phw_default_palette()). A key then keeps a second set of colours, stored as name@accessible, with the groups in the same order. So the same report can be rendered in default and in accessible colours, and each version keeps its colours from one run to the next.

"main" carries on into "extended" after four groups. When a palette runs out altogether, the key carries on with unused colours from the other PHW palettes, then lighter tints, and warns you. "extended" keeps twelve colours apart, but past about eight groups a chart is hard to read by colour alone: use facets, direct labels or scale_shape_phw() as well.

Groups called "Other", "Unknown", "Not known" and similar are drawn in grey so they don't compete with real groups. Change this with neutral.

See also

scale_colour_phw_d() with key = "name" to use a key in ggplot2. The returned vector also works directly in plotly (colors =), flextable and reactable.

Examples

ages <- c("0-4", "5-14", "15-44", "45-64", "65+")
phw_colour_key(ages, "age_example")
#>       0-4      5-14     15-44     45-64       65+ 
#> "#285087" "#24A2B5" "#FF5D0C" "#F43882" "#231F20" 
# A new band keeps the others where they were:
phw_colour_key(c(ages, "Unknown", "85+"), "age_example")
#>       0-4      5-14     15-44     45-64       65+   Unknown       85+ 
#> "#285087" "#24A2B5" "#FF5D0C" "#F43882" "#231F20" "#768692" "#338276" 
phw_key_reset("age_example")
